world.title: US Midterm Elections 2026 Live Updates Donald Trump JD Vance Democrats Republicans Senate House
world.summary: Polling stations opened in Gaithersburg, Maryland, for the 2026 US midterm elections, marking a significant moment for both major parties. Voter sentiment appears to be shifting against the Republican Party, serving as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency. Many voters expressed hopes for political change, citing concerns over rising taxes and other pressing issues as they cast their ballots.

world.title: US Midterms: Why Do Americans Vote On A Tuesday? The 180-Year-Old Horse-And-Buggy Story Behind Election Day
world.summary: Voting in the U.S. occurs on Tuesdays, a practice established 180 years ago to accommodate 19th-century farmers. Critics contend this scheduling poses challenges for contemporary working families, who find it difficult to vote during standard work hours. The debate highlights the need for potential reforms to make voting more accessible for all citizens in today's society.

world.title: QS World University Rankings 2027: India Leads Asia In Research Output
world.summary: The QS World University Rankings 2027 report indicates that India leads Asia in research output, attributed to its exceptional doctoral capacity. Released by Quacquarelli Symonds on November 3, 2026, the rankings show India as the second most represented higher education system in Asia. The report highlights India's significant contributions to academic research and its growing influence in the region.

business.title: NSE's Q2 profit jumps 23% to Rs 2,578 crore in first earnings show post-listing
business.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) reported a consolidated profit of Rs 2,578 crore for the quarter ending September 30, marking a 23% increase from Rs 2,098 crore in the same period last year. This growth was primarily driven by the performance of its trading segment, reflecting strong market activity following its recent listing.

business.title: Q2 Results 03rd Nov Oct Live: SBI Q2 PAT up 14%, Bajaj Finserv, Pfizer, Solar Ind, Rane (Madras), Yatharth, Emcure Pharma & Zydus Wellness Q2 profit rise, AIA Engineering profit declines, NSE, Fortis,
business.summary: On November 3, 2026, several companies reported their Q2 results. State Bank of India (SBI) saw a 14% increase in profit after tax. Other notable profit increases were reported by Bajaj Finserv, Pfizer, Solar Industries, Rane (Madras), Yatharth, Emcure Pharma, and Zydus Wellness. AIA Engineering experienced a decline in profit. Live updates covered numerous companies' financial performances.

business.title: Air India eyes more widebodies, cost cuts under new CEO
business.summary: Air India aims to expand its widebody fleet and implement aggressive cost-cutting measures to enhance profitability under new CEO Tewolde Gebremariam. The airline is focused on increasing its widebody orders to align with its network and strategic goals. Gebremariam emphasized the urgency of achieving profitability “as soon as possible” as part of the company’s future plans.

technology.title: PlayStation Store's Black Friday 2026 Deals Revealed with Games Like Wolverine, and More
technology.summary: PlayStation has announced its Black Friday 2026 deals, starting earlier than usual on November 4, 2026. The sale will feature discounts on various games, including titles like Wolverine. The official PlayStation X account shared the details, highlighting the anticipated offers available on the PlayStation Store. Gamers can look forward to significant savings during this promotional event.

technology.title: EXCLUSIVE: KTM 490 Duke And Adventure Launch Timeline Revealed; RC450 Showcased At EICMA 2026
technology.summary: KTM showcased the RC450 at EICMA 2026, highlighting its new middleweight sportbike. The RC450 is based on the CFMoto platform. Additionally, KTM is developing the 490 Duke and 490 Adventure, which will be built on a new India-made platform. These models aim to expand KTM's offerings in the middleweight motorcycle segment in the near future.

technology.title: Anthropic adds new rule to Claude Code for game clones; company says: Using Claude to infringe IP is against our...
technology.summary: Anthropic has implemented a new rule in Claude Code that prohibits the AI coding tool from recreating existing video games, regardless of whether users rename them or claim originality. This measure aims to prevent intellectual property infringement. The update applies to both Claude Code and Opus 5.5, reinforcing the company's stance against using its tools for unauthorized game cloning.

sports.title: Up 53 spots! Vaishnavi Sharma makes giant leap in ICC ODI rankings after stunning spells against Zimbabwe
sports.summary: Vaishnavi Sharma has risen 53 places in the ICC Women's ODI Player Rankings following India's 3-0 clean sweep against Zimbabwe in the recent three-match series. Her impressive performances as a young spinner have garnered attention, contributing to her significant leap in the rankings. The series showcased several players, highlighting India's strong showing in women's cricket.

sports.title: Harmer calls on 'genius' Carl Crowe to boost English spin prowess
sports.summary: Simon Harmer has called for the appointment of Carl Crowe to enhance England's spin bowling capabilities. Harmer, a spinner for South Africa and Essex, emphasized that Jack Leach is currently England's most reliable option for the Test team. He believes that the development of English spinners is hindered by insufficient specialized coaching resources available to them.

sports.title: 'Past players will start to go at them': Ex-England cricketer warns Australia ahead of 2027 Ashes
sports.summary: Former England cricketer Michael Atherton has stated that England has a strong chance to pressure Australia during their upcoming white-ball tour. He noted that Australia's recent struggles and selection issues could be advantageous for England. Atherton emphasized that past players may begin to challenge Australia more aggressively, suggesting a shift in dynamics for the 2027 Ashes series.

health.title: 4 easy habits to incorporate into your daily routine to boost lymphatic drainage
health.summary: Incorporating daily habits can enhance lymphatic drainage, supporting immunity and overall health. Dr. Gerald M. Lemole emphasizes the importance of lymph in his book, highlighting its essential functions. Four expert-recommended habits include staying hydrated, regular exercise, deep breathing techniques, and incorporating lymphatic massage. These practices aim to improve lymphatic flow, contributing to longevity and vitality in daily life.

health.title: Man's warning over symptoms of leg condition
health.summary: Paul Hardy, diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) four years ago, experienced severe pain prompting his diagnosis. He emphasizes the serious risks associated with the condition, including potential limb loss. To manage his PAD, Hardy underwent angioplasty procedures aimed at improving blood flow to his legs. He warns others about recognizing symptoms to prevent similar outcomes.

health.title: Man's warning over symptoms of peripheral arterial disease
health.summary: Paul Hardy, diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) four years ago, experienced severe pain prompting his diagnosis. He emphasizes the serious risks associated with PAD, including potential limb loss. To manage his condition, Hardy underwent angioplasty procedures aimed at improving blood flow to his legs. He aims to raise awareness about PAD symptoms and the importance of early intervention.

science.title: NASA Telescope To Fall On Earth: Mumbai, Hyderabad In Possible Debris Zone
science.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a 1.5-tonne space telescope launched on November 20, 2004, is set to re-enter Earth's atmosphere. Originally designed for a two-year mission, it operated for nearly 22 years, observing over 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 supernovae. Mumbai and Hyderabad are identified as potential debris zones during its descent.

science.title: 100 billion times smaller than atom, scientists explore 'zeptoverse'
science.summary: Scientists have detected signals from the smallest scale of nature, approximately 100 billion times smaller than an atom, termed the 'zeptoverse.' This discovery opens new avenues for understanding fundamental physics and the universe's structure. Researchers believe that exploring this scale could lead to significant advancements in various scientific fields, enhancing our comprehension of the natural world.

science.title: Astronauts Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk to install the last ISS roll-out solar array on Thursday: All you need to know about the spacewalk
science.summary: Astronauts Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk will conduct a spacewalk on November 5 to install the final roll-out solar array on the International Space Station (ISS). This installation marks the completion of nearly ten years of work and is expected to increase the ISS's power generation capacity by approximately 30%, enhancing its operational capabilities in space.

entertainment.title: Amitabh Bachchan drops health update after expressing he's been advised to take a break: 'Gyming has been a bit non routined, don't let the old man in'
entertainment.summary: Amitabh Bachchan shared a health update, revealing he has been advised to take a break. He mentioned difficulties with sleep and the need to establish a consistent gym routine. Despite these challenges, he encourages his fans not to succumb to aging, stating, "don't let the old man in." Bachchan frequently updates fans about his life through his blog and X.

entertainment.title: Amitabh Bachchan Opens Up About Sleep Struggles At 84, Shares Fitness Mantra
entertainment.summary: Amitabh Bachchan, at 84, discussed his struggles with sleep and maintaining his fitness routine due to a demanding work schedule. The veteran actor highlighted how his busy commitments have impacted his gym sessions. Despite these challenges, he continues to focus on his health and fitness, emphasizing the importance of staying active and managing time effectively.

entertainment.title: Ranbir Kapoor reacts to the mixed early reviews to 'Ramayana': 'Kuchh to log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna'
entertainment.summary: Ranbir Kapoor addressed the mixed early reviews of Nitesh Tiwari's adaptation of the 'Ramayana,' stating, "Kuchh to log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna." The film has garnered attention since its teaser release earlier this year and is scheduled to premiere in cinemas worldwide on November 5. The project aims to present a fresh interpretation of the Indian epic.
